key_insight: Faithful synthetic survival data can support consistent Cox model estimates under stated conditions, but valid inference requires more than distributional fidelity.
engineering_relevance: TSGSurv offers a framework for generating censored time-to-event data for biomedical data sharing, trial simulation, and digital twins.
method: Use a two-stage generator for observed times and covariates conditional on event status.
Establish distributional convergence rates and conditions for consistent Cox coefficient estimates.
Correct variance and calibrate distributions to recover valid inference for the original data.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive simulations and two real-data applications evaluating the generative and inferential framework.
watch_item: Naive inference from synthetic data can be unreliable; validity depends on theoretical conditions and appropriate inferential corrections.
paper_title: Faithful Generative Modeling for Censored Time-to-Event Data: From Distributional Fidelity to Statistical Inference
